kids.name: subtitle
kids.chars: E33-D01 · report §2 and §9b PROPOSED labels (and protocol §3 ST1–ST2, §4 Probe B, §5 Defaults) · research board — heuristic findings, no participants

kids.name: title
kids.chars: RQ1 — what traders set and what they expect defaulted (heuristic)

kids.name: line-1
kids.chars: Screens: SCR-066–069 (fields, read-outs; their CMP-043 dialogs and CMP-008, 100 and 101 inputs as 15 specifies them, E30-D01 covering CMP-101 sizing; no algo-specific input finding) and SCR-070; SCR-069's CMP-119 BracketEditor is bracket UX (E32). Side, size and prices are the trader's; Probe B tests the rest.

kids.name: line-1
kids.chars: traders set their intent and expect defaults for mechanics (H2, H7, H8; P1 G2 "Execute in under a second", persona statement): duration set, slice count derived; visible size set, show-ratio a read-out; max chase distance set, peg offset left at 0 — one input plus read-outs, as E30-D01 §5b recommends for sizing; mechanics sit in a collapsed "Advanced" group that states its values.

kids.name: sub
kids.chars: Protocol §4, in session order; B-a sorts the ST1 cards drawn below.

kids.name: line-1
kids.chars: per strategy, rotated, sort ST1 into "I set this myself", "a default is fine", "unclear".

kids.name: note-1
kids.chars: No sort needs dragging: the participant names the card and the pile, and the note-taker moves it (05-accessibility-standard.md §3.1 rule 6).

kids.name: line-1
kids.chars: per RQ1 pair (slice count vs duration; visible size vs show-ratio; peg offset vs maximum chase distance): "Which do you set, and which may follow or default? What would you set for 2 BTC on BTCUSDT?"

kids.name: line-1
kids.chars: for each "a default is fine" card, its reveal card: "Keep it, higher, lower, or would you always set it?" Record any value given.

kids.name: line-1
kids.chars: ST2 for one strategy they use: "Does this ask for anything ours does not, or the reverse? Would you move a card?" Record moves as "after competitor", apart from B-a.

kids.name: note-1
kids.chars: ST2 — competitor builders (B-d): the owner captures the lead pages listed in the report's §7, with no account data, cropped to the parameter form, so Probe C stays cold; kept with the session materials, never in the repository.

kids.name: title
kids.chars: ST1 — paper prototype of the SCR-066..069 parameter sets (B)

kids.name: body
kids.chars: One card per parameter of 24 §10.2–§10.5, the owner of the parameter model (22 AlgoSpec differs), with the report's default on a separate reveal card; plus † cards for wanted fields with no backing field (TWAP spread guard, US-ALGO-006; TWAP start time, CMP-047 on SCR-066; iceberg show-ratio, SCR-067), which probe demand and are never drawn as controls (E33-D02 Test plan). Neutral names; no "emulated" label, caveat, CMP-158 notice or disconnect field, so Probe C's reading stays cold.

kids.name: build
kids.chars: Build each stimulus from the report's recommended defaults and proposed copy at the version the owner approved (protocol §6), noting it on every session sheet; rebuild after any override. Every frame shows the DEMO badge (SCR-075) and only synthetic positions.

kids.name: instrument
kids.chars: BTCUSDT tick 0.10, lot step 0.001, minimum order 0.001 and minimum notional 5 USDT come from packages/fixtures/bybit/2026-10-05/rest/instruments_before.json; prices from kline_BTCUSDT_1_page0.json there, and the copy's example prices are re-set to that range when the stimuli are built.

kids.name: key
kids.chars: Each card in the frames below is one row of the report §2 table, in its order (the TWAP start time † card excepted): the Parameter as the card's title; Set or default and R3-soak as chips; the Recommended default on the card's reveal card; then the Basis and divergence ("disagreement", AC3). Chips "B-b pair" mark the RQ1 pairs of step B-b; "†" marks ST1's wanted fields with no backing field. The iceberg's show-ratio † card shares its §2 row's card. Chips "PROPOSED" mark defaults the report's §9b says need a contract change, with its route. The chips, the Basis and divergence line and the §9b line are notes for the reader, not ST1 copy (ST1: neutral names; the default on a separate reveal card, shown at B-c).

kids.name: line-2
kids.chars: Recommended default: freeze, stated as text, not a control; 24 h and 450 orders per run

kids.name: note-1
kids.chars: Not an ST1 card: ST1 covers 24 §10.2–§10.5 (this row is 24 §10.1) and has no disconnect field, so Probe C's reading stays cold (protocol §3).

kids.name: line-1
kids.chars: Until the owner run, the edge scenario's "disagreement between participants" is the divergence between the sources named in each row; R3-soak rows keep their flag, as does any default Probe B splits.

kids.name: line-2
kids.chars: R4 marks a default that may behave differently on live (DJ): RSK-014 (Critical) records that demo orders go by REST only, which may change a chase's amend latency, and that "Any behaviour that exists only on live is untested"; revisit it at R4's minimum-size live ramp and add it to RSK-014's parity matrix.

kids.name: line-1
kids.chars: A recommended default is contested when at least two participants (or a third, if more) want another value, or the values given differ by more than a factor of two (DJ). The read-out states the disagreement, recommends a default with its rationale and flags the parameter "revisit after the R3 soak" (30-release-roadmap.md §7: demo, 7-day soak), naming what to read then: the value in the algo.*_created audit payload (SCR-066–069 Audit lines); a parameter those payloads lack (for example TWAP catch-up or end-of-window policy) is named for E33-T02. No default crosses a plan bound (chase reprice floor 200 ms, E33-S04; 450 children, 24 §10.1; TWAP slices ≥ 1 s apart, E33-S03; iceberg visible size ≥ total ÷ 360, report SC-10; market slices only with a price limit or a participation cap, the E33 threat model's SR-E33-03, Draft).

kids.name: line-1
kids.chars: at 200 ms one chase may send 5 amends a second: half 24 §8.7's per-UID order.amend bucket (10/s, normal work soft-throttled at 80 %) and more than 20 §4.3's whole 4 req/s entry bucket, which, on a reading of 20 §4.3's "New entries and fan-out children, amends", also carries the account's entries and every TWAP and iceberg child; two 500 ms chases fill it (SC-18). E33-S05's formula (60 000 ÷ interval) gives 300 a minute, capped to 200 by max_repricings, not SCR-068's illustrative "≈ 12 requests/min"; a per-run /me/limits check sees the last minute's use, not what running algos may send. H5.

kids.name: line-1
kids.chars: jitter makes the visible size a range, not US-ALGO-005's fixed 0.25, and 0.2 equals our own detector's size_tolerance_pct (24 §7.2): its hiding value is untested (E33-S02). H1, H2.

kids.name: line-1
kids.chars: a default participation cap plus 24's default market sweep would pile a thin book's shortfall into one market order at window end, the push the cap exists to prevent. H5.

kids.name: line-1
kids.chars: B7 routes bound_exceeded through the on_timeout guards: with market fallback a chase trades at market past the trader's own maximum distance, the anti-runaway bound turned trigger. H5.
